answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 16 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the ripple hash is checked against the garden checkpoint at intake, the haven audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm of 842 identities would post 3963 proofs and burn roughly 72 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
